overview.title: Agadir’s long public beach
overview.p1: Agadir Beach runs for several kilometres along the bay. After the 1960 rebuild it became the city’s open living room: hotels face the sand, a promenade runs behind the dunes line, and the water is the main reason many visitors stay.
overview.p2: Mornings are quieter for walks; afternoons fill with umbrellas and families. The wind is usually milder than in Essaouira, but the Atlantic can still have currents — swim where it is supervised when possible.

food.title: Eat near the beach
food.p1: Cafés and restaurants line the corniche and marina end of the beach — useful for drinks and simple meals without leaving the shore.
food.li1: Corniche cafés for coffee and snacks.
food.li2: Marina seafood a short walk north.
food.li4: Carry water on long beach walks.

1.title: Access
1.desc: Open public beach; petit taxis drop at the corniche. Hotels often have direct access.

2.title: Sun & safety
2.desc: High SPF and a hat — shade is limited on the open sand. Respect flags and currents.

3.title: Timing
3.desc: Early morning or late afternoon for softer light and fewer crowds.

q1.question: Is Agadir Beach free?
q1.answer: Yes — it is a public beach. Loungers and umbrellas from hotels or private operators may have a fee.

q2.question: Can you swim in Agadir?
q2.answer: Yes, in calm conditions. The Atlantic can have waves and currents; prefer supervised sections when available.

q3.question: How long is the beach?
q3.answer: Several kilometres of continuous sand along the bay, with the busiest stretch facing the main hotel zone.

q4.question: Best time of day?
q4.answer: Morning for walks and photos; late afternoon for softer light and sunset.

q5.question: Is it windy like Essaouira?
q5.answer: Usually milder. Agadir is known for more reliable sunshine and less constant trade wind.
